name: Korban Tamid — Detailed Procedure
notes: Detailed step-by-step procedure of the daily tamid offering as described in tractate Tamid: slaughter, blood sprinkling, flaying, limb division, and bringing to the altar

name: Temple Night Watch (Mishmar HaLaylah)
notes: Laws and practice of the priestly night watch in the Temple courtyard, including the three watch stations: Chamber of Avtinas, Chamber of the Spark, and Chamber of the Hearth

name: Chamber of the Hearth (Beit HaMoked)
notes: The large domed hall in the Temple where priests slept, warmed themselves, and assembled for the lottery; its structure, sleeping arrangements, and role in the daily Temple service

name: Temple Service Lottery (Payis)
notes: The four daily lotteries conducted to assign priests to the various rites of the Temple service, including removal of ashes, slaughter, incense burning, and taking limbs to the altar

name: Removal of Ashes from the Altar (Terumat HaDeshen)
notes: The rite of removing ashes from the outer altar each morning, who performs it, the procedure, and the coal heap in the center of the altar

name: Incense Burning Procedure (Haktarat HaKetoret — Seder)
notes: Detailed procedure for burning the incense on the golden altar, including the coal pan transfer, the spoon and vessel, spreading the incense, and the prohibition on others being present

name: Candelabrum Cleaning and Kindling Procedure
notes: Detailed procedure for removing ashes and wicks from the Candelabrum lamps and rekindling them, including the role of the western lamp and the stone steps before the Candelabrum

name: Arrangement of Wood on the Altar (Ma'arachah)
notes: Laws of assembling the wood arrangements on the outer altar, including which woods are permitted, the large arrangement for offerings, and the second arrangement for incense coals

name: Division and Carrying of Sacrificial Limbs
notes: The precise division of the daily offering's limbs among the priests, the order of carrying them, how they are held, and how they are brought up the ramp to the altar

name: Temple Crier (Gevini HaKorei)
notes: The role of the Temple crier who announced each morning to priests, Levites, and Israelites to take their respective positions for the daily service

name: Temple Sounds Heard in Jericho
notes: Tradition listing the sounds and smells of the Temple service that were perceptible from as far as Jericho, including the gate, shovel, Basin pulley, shofar, cymbals, and incense

name: Ben Katin's Basin Mechanism (Mukhani)
notes: The pulley mechanism crafted by Ben Katin to submerge the Basin overnight so its water would not be disqualified by remaining still, and the sound it made when raised

name: Priestly Immersion Passage Under the Temple
notes: The underground passage allowing an impure priest to exit to the Chamber of Immersion without passing through the Temple courtyard, including the bathroom and immersion facilities there

name: Recitation of Ten Commandments in the Temple
notes: The daily practice of the priestly watch in the Chamber of Hewn Stone to recite the Ten Commandments along with the Shema and its blessings

name: Differences in Priestly Blessing in the Temple
notes: Distinctions between the Priestly Benediction as performed in the Temple vs. outside: recited as one blessing, use of the divine name as written, hands raised above the head, and the response formula

name: Daily Psalm of the Levites (Shir shel Yom)
notes: The assignment of specific psalms to each day of the week, recited by the Levites during the daily wine libation, as listed at the end of tractate Tamid

name: Temple Slaughterhouse and Rings (Beit HaMitbachayim)
notes: The northern slaughterhouse area of the Temple with its twenty-four rings affixed to the floor for holding animals during slaughter, the pillars, hooks, and marble tables

name: High Priest's Prerogative to Sacrifice Any Offering
hebrew: זכות הכהן הגדול להקריב בכל עת
notes: The High Priest's right to offer any portion of any sacrifice he wishes at any time, and the procedure by which he receives the limbs from other priests and places his hands upon them

name: Deputy High Priest (Segan HaKohanim)
notes: The role of the deputy high priest (segan) in assisting the High Priest, standing to his right, signaling the Levites with cloths during the libation, and other functions

name: Trumpet and Cymbal Signal for Libation and Levitical Song
notes: The procedure of sounding trumpets (tekia, terua, tekia) and clashing cymbals by Ben Arza to signal the start of the Levitical psalm during the libation, and the people's prostration at each section

name: Chamber of Hewn Stone (Lishkat HaGazit)
notes: The Chamber of Hewn Stone where lotteries were conducted and the priests recited Shema and its blessings each morning before the daily service

name: Temple Shovel Sound (Magreifah)
notes: The instrument thrown between the Entrance Hall and the altar that produced a sound so loud no voice could be heard in Jerusalem, signaling priests, Levites, and the non-priestly watch to assemble

name: Pesakhter (Large Ash Vessel)
notes: A large vessel holding a half-kor used to remove ashes from the altar, to cover scattered coals on Shabbat, and to cover a dead creeping animal found in the Temple on Shabbat
